A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original simulations in Figure 3, including Beta-distributed vectors and beta/binomial mixtures, with variability across 100 trials.

after.justification: v5 retains these original simulation results in Figure 3 and Appendix E, including standard deviations across 100 trials.

M1.justification: v4 uses the uniform-distribution construction for general sub-ψ confidence spheres. v5 restricts it to super-Gaussian ψ and introduces a von Mises-Fisher construction for general ψ in Theorem A.3, producing a different confidence radius.

E1.justification: The same bound-comparison scenarios and bounded-vector simulations are retained. The broader theoretical discussion does not introduce additional datasets or evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Figures 1–3 retain the Hsu et al. bound, geometric and tournament median-of-means methods, and oracle Bernstein comparisons, with the same sequentialization variants. The new Table 2 compares theoretical guarantees without adding simulation baselines.

E3.justification: Simulation Details, moved from Appendix C to Appendix D, retain the same parameter choices, covariance settings, and union-bound and doubling procedures. The plotted evaluation ranges are unchanged.

E4.justification: The covariance-ratio comparisons in Figure 1 and variance-adaptation and asymptotic-width simulations in Figure 3 are unchanged. No additional empirical sensitivity, robustness, or ablation analyses appear.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains standard-deviation shading across 100 trials. No repeated-run, seed, or experimental uncertainty-reporting practices change.

E6.justification: All six plot panels in Figures 1–3 are identical across versions, and their reported rankings and trends are retained. No empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: v5 adds the super-Gaussian definition, Lemma 2.10 establishing extension from the sphere to the ball, and Theorem A.3 with supporting von Mises-Fisher lemmas C.2–C.3. It also corrects the truncated-Gaussian KL calculation and a missing square in the proof of Theorem 3.5, adds an α ≤ 2/e qualification, and corrects the ellipsoid formula to use the ordinary sample mean.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 3 now distinguishes Theorem 2.12 for super-Gaussian ψ from Theorem A.3 for general ψ, qualifying the earlier claim of generality for Theorem 2.12. The other principal contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v5 explains why non-super-Gaussian ψ requires sphere-supported mixing and warns that the resulting bound typically has worse dimension dependence and constants. It recommends the tighter Theorem 2.12 when its assumptions hold.

D1.justification: The code-access information and simulation implementation recipes are retained in the relocated Simulation Details appendix. No additional experimental implementation or resource information is disclosed.

R1.justification: v5 adds directional-statistics and application references, introduces a comparison with Maurer and Pontil (2021), and expands discussion of Manole and Ramdas (2023). Table 2 organizes relationships to prior bounds while preserving the main research positioning.

P1.justification: v5 adds a worked PAC-Bayesian example in Section 1.2, revises parts of Section 2.3, and moves the isotropic example and two fixed-time corollaries into Appendix A. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds the theoretical-comparison Table 2 and updates Table 1 references. Figures and surrounding text are reflowed, but Figures 1–3 retain identical plot images.

improvement.justification: v5 addresses an important gap in a main theoretical contribution: it states and proves the condition needed for the sphere-to-ball argument and supplies a separate construction for general ψ (Section 2.3 and Appendix A.3). This substantially improves the justification and applicability guidance for the confidence guarantees. The general bound is looser, but that tradeoff is explicit; the existing simulation evidence is preserved.
